answer: The design that broke did everything right on paper, scoring behaviour, flagging clusters and banning on threshold, and it still lost, for one structural reason: behavioural clustering fails because staggering posts defeats it at almost no cost. What survives is boring and numeric: a 64-kilobyte unique shard re-sampled at 12 random blocks. Start here: the plume outlives the account that produced it. Underneath it all, put plainly, privilege should unlock at a measured zenith, not at signup. Remember that a farm can forge the label but not the vine.
